items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That plus what Page and all the bassists that followed there... We used to call it a 'ching' and a 'chang.' ... He would start off playing a tune, 'plink,' and Page and Jo Jones, 'cha-boom bing doom ssh-sh-sssssh,' and Basie say, 'plink cha-plink,'

ctx.x: What was Jo Jones, Freddie Green, that rhythm section like to play with in the first band, when you first got there?

It was very – like a well-oiled machine, something that was so fitting and so beautiful, ’til you could just relax. It’s like sitting back in your most comfortable chair at home, just sitting back and relaxing, because you could play, because you knew that they had you. You could relax. You could lay back. That was the – one of the prime prerequisites to play in the Basie band, to be able to lay back and relax, and with a rhythm section like that, you could do that, because Freddie Green has a system of playing…
around and just make it swing and then come back. And Basie was phenomenal at comping. He knew how to play and leave just enough space for you to kill yourself.
